stories.title: Bitget Confirms $388 Million Security Breach, Offers Bounty for Stolen Funds
stories.summary: Bitget confirmed a security breach on its hot wallets. The exchange first put the loss near $352 million. It later revised the figure up to about $388 million. Bitget suspended withdrawals and set a bounty for the return of the stolen crypto.
stories.whyItMatters: Large exchange breaches test user trust in centralized custody and often trigger wider scrutiny of exchange security practices.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitget resumes withdrawals
Whether the bounty leads to recovered funds
Any further revision of the breach total
questions: Will Bitget reimburse affected users in full?

stories.title: CFTC Weighs Single-Stock Perpetual Futures, Eases Tokenized-Asset Rules
stories.summary: Trading platform OG.com asked the CFTC to approve single-stock perpetual futures contracts. Separately, the CFTC issued updated guidance that lets U.S. commodities firms invest in tokenized assets and use blockchain records. The guidance came shortly after a related vote failed.
stories.whyItMatters: Both moves show U.S. regulators continuing to open paths for tokenization and derivatives products, which could widen institutional access to crypto-linked instruments.
whatToWatch: The CFTC's decision on OG.com's application
Further guidance following the failed vote
questions: Why did the earlier vote fail?
Will other trading platforms file similar requests?

stories.title: Bitcoin Could Gain Zcash-Style Shielded Privacy Without a Rule Change
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports that developers are exploring a way to add Zcash-style shielded privacy to Bitcoin. The approach would not require a change to Bitcoin's core consensus rules. Details on the method and who is building it remain limited.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin privacy tools are a long-running point of debate; a path that avoids a contentious rule change could shift that discussion.
whatToWatch: Technical details as the proposal develops
Reaction from Bitcoin core developers
questions: Who is developing this, and on what timeline?
How would it affect exchange compliance requirements?

stories.title: Wall Street and Crypto Firms Compete for the Same Business
stories.summary: Cointelegraph's Crypto Biz roundup covers how Wall Street institutions and crypto-native firms increasingly push into the same products and services. The piece is a broad industry roundup rather than a report on one single event.
stories.whyItMatters: The blurring line between traditional finance and crypto shapes where liquidity, talent, and regulatory attention go next.
questions: Which firms or products sit at the center of this rivalry?

stories.title: Whitehats Rescue 3,832 NFTs Worth $5.7M From Magic Eden Exploit Risk
stories.summary: Old, unrevoked token approvals on NFT marketplace Magic Eden left about $5.7 million in NFTs open to an exploit. Whitehat researchers moved roughly 3,832 of the exposed NFTs into protective custody before an attacker could take them.
stories.whyItMatters: The incident shows how old approval permissions stay a real risk across NFT and DeFi platforms long after users forget about them.
whatToWatch: Whether Magic Eden helps users revoke remaining old approvals
Return of the rescued NFTs to their owners
questions: How long had the exposed approvals existed before discovery?

stories.title: Bitcoin ETF Flows Turn Positive for 2026 After Erasing $5.8B Deficit
stories.summary: Cumulative 2026 flows into U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs turned positive. A six-day inflow streak totaling $2.8 billion erased an earlier $5.8 billion deficit. The daily pace slowed to $191 million on the most recent day.
stories.whyItMatters: ETF flows are a key read on institutional demand, and this swing from deficit to positive suggests renewed appetite after a weak stretch.
whatToWatch: Whether the inflow streak continues or reverses
Next weekly flow totals across issuers
questions: What caused the earlier deficit, and has that condition changed?

stories.title: Bitcoin Holders Take Profits, But Not Like They Did at Past Market Tops
stories.summary: On-chain data cited by CoinDesk shows long-term bitcoin holders taking profits. The selling pattern differs from what was seen at prior market peaks. Separately, CryptoSlate notes bitcoin faces a fresh inflation test after diesel prices hit a nominal record of $6.53.
stories.whyItMatters: Reading this selling pattern correctly matters for judging whether bitcoin's cycle is peaking, and rising fuel costs could add pressure on risk assets generally.
whatToWatch: Whether holder selling speeds up or steadies
Upcoming inflation data releases
questions: Does this selling pattern signal a market top, or just routine profit-taking?

stories.title: KelpDAO Sues LayerZero Over $292M rsETH Exploit, One of 2026's Largest
stories.summary: KelpDAO filed a lawsuit against LayerZero and its CEO. KelpDAO claims LayerZero endorsed a bridge setup that was later used in a $292 million exploit of its rsETH token. The Block and CoinDesk both call it the largest crypto exploit so far in 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: The suit could set a precedent for how much liability infrastructure providers bear when a setup they endorsed gets exploited.
whatToWatch: LayerZero's response to the lawsuit
Whether any of the stolen funds are recovered
questions: What exactly did LayerZero endorse, and did it know the risk?
Will other protocols using similar bridge setups face scrutiny?

stories.title: US Crypto ETFs Draw Over $3B This Week, Nearly $800M Beyond Bitcoin
stories.summary: U.S. crypto ETFs took in more than $3 billion in inflows this week. Almost $800 million of that went into products beyond Bitcoin, according to CryptoSlate.
stories.whyItMatters: Growing inflows into non-Bitcoin crypto ETFs suggest institutional demand is spreading beyond the largest cryptocurrency.
whatToWatch: Which non-Bitcoin products draw the most flow
Whether the broadening trend holds next week
questions: Which specific assets are driving the non-Bitcoin inflows?

stories.title: SEC Issues Crypto FAQ on Token Buybacks, Network Upgrades, Profit Promises
stories.summary: The SEC published a FAQ on how securities law applies to crypto token buybacks, network upgrades, and promises of profit. The Block reports the FAQ gives informal guidance rather than a formal rule.
stories.whyItMatters: The FAQ gives projects and issuers a clearer sense of where the SEC currently draws its enforcement lines.
whatToWatch: Whether projects adjust practices in response
Whether the FAQ leads to formal rulemaking
questions: Does the FAQ carry binding legal weight, or is it purely informal guidance?

stories.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs extended their inflow streak, adding nearly $3 billion, according to Bitcoin Magazine. The report adds to a broader picture this week of strengthening ETF demand.
stories.whyItMatters: Sustained ETF inflows are a closely watched sign of institutional confidence in bitcoin.
whatToWatch: Whether the streak continues into next week
questions: Which issuers are capturing most of these inflows?

stories.title: Ex-CFTC Leader to Leave Blockchain Association After CLARITY Vote Fails
stories.summary: A former CFTC leader plans to leave the Blockchain Association. The departure follows the failure of a vote on the CLARITY Act, Cointelegraph reports. Details on the reasons and next steps are limited.
stories.whyItMatters: Leadership turnover at a major crypto lobbying group, tied to a failed vote on market-structure legislation, could signal a shift in Washington strategy.

Next steps for the CLARITY Act after the failed vote
questions: Why did the CLARITY vote fail?
